_meta.title: Plugins deliberately NOT in ai-kit catalog
_meta.notes: ai-kit's catalog is for COMPLEMENTARY tools, not ALTERNATIVES that overlap ai-kit's own integrated skills. During initial design (gstack, gsd, superpowers, mattpocock-skills, etc were studied), the best ideas were distilled INTO ai-kit's lifecycle. Recommending these plugins alongside ai-kit creates double-bundle noise. The audit emits KEEP-EXTERNAL with the reason from this file instead of ADOPT, so users see deliberate non-adoption (not 'promotion candidate'). A `reversed` array records verdicts that were overturned, with the evidence that overturned them — an Ignore that quietly disappears is worse than no ledger, because the next person re-litigates it from scratch.

excluded.name: superpowers
excluded.reason: Meta-skill bundle (obra/superpowers-marketplace). Overlaps with ai-kit's /ai:tdd, /ai:review, /ai:retro, /ai:ship, /ai:plan-* and others — best patterns were distilled into ai-kit's own lifecycle during initial design. Adding it as a recommended plugin would create double-bundle noise.
excluded.alternative: Use ai-kit's own lifecycle skills.

excluded.name: taste-skill
excluded.reason: Anti-slop frontend design pack (Leonxlnx/taste-skill, installs via `npx skills add` — not a Claude Code marketplace plugin, so it does not fit the plugins.json schema). Overlaps the existing design entries (frontend-design / lazyweb) and ui-ux-pro-max; single-source preview. Its distinctive value (GSAP motion code skeletons + AI image-board generation) is design *generation*, out of scope for what ai-kit recommends as durable per-project infra. should-i-use verdict: Ignore.
excluded.alternative: If a project specifically wants its motion/image-board generation, install directly: `npx skills add https://github.com/Leonxlnx/taste-skill`. Use ui-ux-pro-max for reasoned design-system output.

excluded.name: designlang
excluded.reason: Live-DOM design-system EXTRACTION tool (Manavarya09/design-extract, npm `designlang`). Ships an MCP server + Claude Code plugin, so it is structurally eligible for the mcp-servers.json bucket — but it optimizes none of the AI-loop dimensions the companion catalog is for (graphify=input, caveman=output, llm-wiki=memory, context7=docs); it emits frontend artefacts (DTCG tokens / Tailwind / shadcn / Figma) from a URL. That is one-shot task tooling you run when cloning/matching a design, not durable per-project infra that compounds each session. Fails the promotion-quorum bar (single-maintainer, v12.23 high-churn, sponsor-affiliate README → 1 source, preview-only, never default-recommended). Same out-of-scope bucket as taste-skill (design generation/extraction). should-i-use verdict: Ignore.
excluded.alternative: If a frontend project genuinely needs live-site token extraction or CI drift-check against a deployed source-of-truth, install directly and wire its MCP: `npx designlang <url>` / `designlang mcp`. Use ui-ux-pro-max for reasoned design-system output.

excluded.name: codebase-memory-mcp
excluded.reason: Code-intelligence MCP server (DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp, pure-C static binary, MIT). Builds a persistent knowledge graph via tree-sitter (158 langs) + 'Hybrid LSP' type resolution; 14 MCP tools (search_graph, trace_path, Cypher query_graph, semantic search, cross-service HTTP linking). Structurally eligible for the mcp-servers.json bucket, but it is an ALTERNATIVE to graphify (ai-kit's knowledge-graph/input companion, wired into CLAUDE.md + query workflow + PreToolUse hook) — not complementary. Its own README says it is 'similar in spirit to graphify's graphify-out/'. Two knowledge-graph tools = double-bundle noise. Adopting it also runs against ADR-0006 (ai-kit deliberately dropped MCP; stays pure Bash+Markdown, minimal footprint) and its curl|bash install auto-wires config + hooks across 11 agents. Fails promotion-quorum like designlang/taste-skill: single org, README = sole source. should-i-use verdict: Ignore. Whether it should REPLACE graphify (stronger engine on paper) is a separate deliberate spike, not a catalog add — tracked in #109.
excluded.alternative: Keep graphify as the knowledge-graph companion. If a project specifically wants type-aware call graphs / semantic / Cypher search, install directly and wire its MCP per the upstream README. Migration decision: see issue #109.

excluded.name: headroom
excluded.reason: Context-compression layer for AI agents (headroomlabs-ai/headroom, Apache-2.0, ~47k stars, active). Proxy + MCP + library that compresses tool-outputs/logs/RAG/files 60-95% before the LLM, plus an output-shaper (verbosity steering + effort routing). In-category (token efficiency) and popular — NOT wrong-category like the design tools — but Ignored as a blanket companion on three grounds: (1) footprint vs ADR-0006 — Python 3.10+ + HuggingFace model (Kompress-v2-base) + optional pytorch-mps + long-running proxy, against ai-kit's pure-Bash+Markdown / MCP-dropped / minimal posture; (2) trust surface — the proxy sits in the path of all prompts+responses, exchanges provider/Copilot OAuth tokens, and `headroom learn` auto-edits CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md (the files ai-kit's own loops own); lossy pre-agent compression is a correctness gamble vs ai-kit's verifiability ethos; (3) dimension-spanning overlap — its output-shaper dubbelt caveman, its cross-agent memory/learn dubbelt llm-wiki + the checkpoint loop. Only its proxy tool-output compression is genuinely new (graphify indexes code, not a 65k-token log). should-i-use verdict: Ignore. Whether that one novel angle earns a 'runtime-output' companion entry is a separate deliberate spike, not a catalog add — tracked in #110.
excluded.alternative: Keep graphify (code input) + caveman (output) as the orthogonal companions. If a specific project drowns in large runtime tool-outputs (SRE logs, big grep/RAG dumps) AND accepts the proxy trust surface, install directly and wire its MCP per upstream: `pip install headroom-ai[all]` / `headroom mcp install`. Adoption decision: see issue #110.

excluded.name: skillspector
excluded.reason: Security scanner for AI agent skills (NVIDIA/SkillSpector, Apache-2.0, Python 3.12+). 68 vuln patterns across 17 categories (prompt injection, data exfiltration, privilege escalation, supply chain, MCP tool poisoning, …), two-stage static + optional-LLM, SARIF/JSON/MD output, scans repo/URL/zip/dir/file. Ships a CLI + an MCP server (`scan_skill`), so structurally eligible for the mcp-servers.json bucket — but it is one-shot scanner tooling, NOT a per-session compounding companion like the catalog is for (graphify=input, caveman=output, llm-wiki=memory, context7=docs). Footprint (Python + optional-LLM API spend + MCP/long-running scan) runs against ADR-0006 (pure Bash+Markdown, MCP-dropped, no runtime daemon), same posture objection as headroom/codebase-memory-mcp. So it does NOT belong as a recommend-to-everyone companion. UNLIKE the prior Ignores it is neither wrong-category (taste-skill/designlang) nor a duplicate-of-existing-companion (codebase-memory-mcp/headroom): it plugs a real hole in ai-kit's OWN trust machinery — VETTING.md's seven criteria have no automated security/malicious-pattern dimension, yet ai-kit emits 27 skills + recommends 12 plugins under an implicit 'safe to wire' endorsement. NVIDIA-backed + Apache-2.0 clears the single-maintainer/license quorum concerns that sank the others. should-i-use verdict: Ignore (catalog) / Wire-as-internal-tool. Whether to wire `skillspector scan --no-llm` (static, zero-API) as an advisory CI gate on ai-kit's emitted skills + a probe step in should-i-use/recommend-rules is a deliberate spike, not a catalog add — tracked in #111.
excluded.alternative: Don't add to the companion catalog. If wiring as ai-kit's own security gate proves out (#111), it lives in CI + the vetting pipeline, not in a recommend-to-everyone table. To scan a single skill ad-hoc today: `uvx --from git+https://github.com/NVIDIA/skillspector skillspector scan <dir> --no-llm` or via the bundled `scan_skill` MCP tool.

excluded.name: openspec
excluded.reason: Spec-driven planning framework for AI coding agents (Fission-AI/OpenSpec, npm `@fission-ai/openspec`, MIT, Node 20.19+, no MCP / no API keys). `openspec init` creates an `openspec/` tree (changes/<feature>/{proposal,design,tasks}.md + specs/ + archive/) and wires `/opsx:explore|propose|apply|verify|archive` into 30+ agents. Same bucket as `superpowers`: an ALTERNATIVE lifecycle, not a complementary companion. Every stage already has an ai-kit equivalent — explore=grill-me/grill-with-docs, propose=to-prd, tasks=to-issues, apply=tdd+review, archive=ship+retro, design.md=docs/adr/*, cross-session persistence=checkpoint/resume+roadmap.md, specs/=CONTEXT.md+GH issue body. Wiring it forks the command namespace (/ai:* vs /opsx:*) and the contract surface (GH issue with DoR/DoD gates vs openspec/changes/*/tasks.md), and `openspec init` auto-edits AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md — the files ai-kit's own loops own (same objection as headroom). Footprint (global npm + Node) is a mild ADR-0006 hit but not disqualifying on its own; the category overlap is. Promotion-quorum not assessed — single org, README as sole source — because the category rejection is dispositive. should-i-use verdict: Ignore. Its one genuinely novel idea — the requirement delta as an in-repo artifact reviewable in the same PR as the code, where ai-kit's contract surface is deliberately the GH issue body — is a deliberate spike against ai-kit's OWN lifecycle, not a catalog add: tracked in #112.
excluded.alternative: Use ai-kit's own lifecycle skills (grill-with-docs → to-prd → to-issues → tdd → review → ship). If a project specifically wants in-repo spec folders, install directly: `npm install -g @fission-ai/openspec@latest && openspec init` — but do not run it alongside ai-kit's planning skills. Spec-delta-in-diff question: see issue #112.

excluded.name: openwiki
excluded.reason: Agent-written repo documentation CLI (langchain-ai/openwiki, npm `openwiki`, MIT, TypeScript, built on LangChain DeepAgents; 10.4k stars, v0.1.1). An LLM agent reads the repo, writes prose docs into `openwiki/`, appends a pointer block to AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, and keeps itself current off `git log <last-head>..HEAD --name-status` on a scheduled CI job that opens a PR. Two modes: code mode (repo docs) and personal mode (raw sources → wiki, with Gmail/Slack/Notion/X/Tavily connectors). Ignored on category, NOT on trust — LangChain org + MIT + real release clears the single-maintainer/license quorum that sank designlang/taste-skill. Grounds: (1) double overlap — code mode is an ALTERNATIVE to graphify (incl. its `--wiki` tier at graphify-out/wiki/), personal mode is an ALTERNATIVE to llm-wiki (same Karpathy lineage ai-kit already vendored its own schema for); wiring it makes a third `wiki` surface next to the two that already need companions.json's 'Two wikis present — disambiguation' block. (2) For code, it is a strict downgrade vs graphify: LLM-generated prose bakes hallucination to disk and costs API spend per update, where graphify is AST-derived (deterministic, zero cost, incremental via `graphify update .`). (3) ADR-0006 footprint — global npm + Node + DeepAgents runtime + per-update API spend; and it auto-edits AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md, the files ai-kit's own loops own (same objection as headroom and openspec). should-i-use verdict: Ignore. Its one genuinely reusable idea — anchoring a generated artifact to a git head so staleness is COMPUTABLE instead of hoped-for — needed no adoption: graphify already stamps `built_at_commit` into graph.json, and ai-kit now reads it in the docs-sync `graph-fresh` check (v1.47.0), which caught a 34-file/3-commit stale graph in ai-kit itself on first run.
excluded.alternative: Keep graphify (code, AST-derived) + llm-wiki (non-code documents) as the two wiki-shaped companions. Staleness detection ships in `/ai:docs-sync` → graph-fresh (`bin/ai-kit-docs-sync-graph-fresh.sh`); the fix is `graphify update .`, AST-only and free. If a project genuinely wants LLM-written architecture prose with a CI PR gate, install directly per upstream — but do not point it at a repo that already has graphify, and review every generated page before an agent treats it as truth.

excluded.name: technical-writing
excluded.reason: Layered technical-writing skill (pasted SKILL.md, no upstream repo, no licence stated). Stacks four layers: Diataxis document modes, Google developer style, ASD-STE100 instruction rules, and Global English syntax. Three of the four duplicate what ai-kit already ships: the Google, STE and Global English layers restate `writing-style.mini.md` and /ai:copywriter's 39 patterns, down to identical examples (use not utilize, help not facilitate). It also delegates its slop catalogue to an `unslop` skill that does not exist here, and carries `disable-model-invocation: true`, so as a skill it never fires on its own. should-i-use verdict: Ignore as a whole. Its one non-redundant layer, Diataxis, was adopted as a pattern instead: `standards/rules/docs-diataxis.mini.md` (2026-08-20), ~45 lines, on-demand, crediting diataxis.fr.
excluded.alternative: Use `docs-diataxis.mini.md` for document structure, `writing-style.mini.md` for the always-on sentence floor, and /ai:copywriter for the full editor. Do not install the skill alongside them.

excluded.name: unslop
excluded.reason: 31-pattern AI-tell editor (pasted SKILL.md, no upstream repo, no licence stated), marked 'must always apply'. Already inside ai-kit by two routes, so adopting it a third time would triple one source. Patterns 1 to 25 share the same lineage as /ai:copywriter's §1-33, namely Wikipedia: Signs of AI writing. Patterns 14, 26, 27, 28, 30 and 31 are the source of `writing-style.mini.md` rules 1 to 6 and of copywriter §34-39: the same jargon list (substrate, wedge, north star, flywheel), the same plain-word list (utilize, facilitate, numerous), and the same mechanism-over-feeling example. Both surfaces now credit it. should-i-use verdict: Ignore. Nothing in it is missing from ai-kit.
excluded.alternative: Use `writing-style.mini.md` (always-on floor) and /ai:copywriter (full 39-pattern editor). Both name unslop in their provenance sections; update those if the upstream list changes.

excluded.name: kakashi
excluded.reason: Local-first PII/secret masker CLI + agent rule (Muhammadatef/kakashi @ 49d51d1cc2044561cfd0771e277e12f69636be1d, MIT, npm @muhammadatef/kakashi 1.0.0). Ignore, on four independent grounds. (1) Wrong control layer: it installs a markdown rule asking the agent to run `kakashi scan` before pasting, but the agent has already read the file into context by then and cannot un-see it; its own README concedes that an @-mention leaks the full body on that turn. Advisory-where-enforcement-is-needed fails open exactly when it matters. ai-kit already catalogs the enforcing version in hooks-patterns.json: `gitleaks-scan` and `block-env-edits`, both PreToolUse/Edit|Write, which the model cannot talk itself out of, plus secrets-hygiene.mini.md prescribing gitleaks pre-commit + CI. (2) Marketing/code parity fails on the headline claim: it advertises .env, but getFormat() keys off path.extname(), which returns '' for `.env` and `.envrc` and '.local'/'.production' for `.env.local`/`.env.production`. Every real dotfile form errors 'Unsupported file format'; only `something.env` works. Verified against this repo's own context/templates/repo/.envrc and tests/fixtures/audit-laravel-*/.env.production. (3) Precision is too low to mask with: the full_name pattern is /\b[A-Z][a-z]+(\s+[A-Z][a-z]+)+\b/ (any TitleCase bigram, matched across newlines), cc is \b\d{13,19}\b, hex_secret is 40+ hex chars. On a 6-line sample doc it returned 7 findings of which 2 were real: 'React Native', 'Release Notes\nBuilt' and 'See Design System' masked as [FULL_NAME_n], a 13-digit epoch-ms timestamp as [CC_1], a pinned git SHA as [HEX_SECRET_1]. Scanning this repo's own standards/rules/secrets-hygiene.mini.md masks 'Secrets Manager' as [FULL_NAME_1]. Credential regexes (db_conn, env_secret, bearer, provider key prefixes) are competent; the PII half is not. (4) Cost and scope: install.sh hardcodes --all, so curl|bash appends a 73-line always-on block to ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, writes ~/.cursor/rules/kakashi.mdc with alwaysApply:true, ~/.codex/AGENTS.md, ~/.windsurf/rules/, mutates ~/.continue/config.json systemMessage, and copies 6 slash commands per agent -- a machine-wide, every-session context tax for a person-scoped concern, which is the shape /ai:dedupe and the context-lean check in /ai:hygiene exist to flag. Also `npm audit`: 2 high, xlsx@0.18.5 prototype-pollution + ReDoS with no fix available (SheetJS left npm) -- a parser aimed at untrusted spreadsheets is the wrong place for that. Maturity: 20 stars, 8 commits, 1 fork, 0 issues, single release 2026-06-04. should-i-use verdict: Ignore.
excluded.alternative: For the enforcement this actually promises, wire the `gitleaks-scan` and `block-env-edits` PreToolUse hooks from hooks-patterns.json via /ai:recommend-tools, and follow secrets-hygiene.mini.md (gitleaks pre-commit + CI, rotate on suspicion). For a genuine one-off need to hand a spreadsheet or PDF to an LLM with names and IDs stripped, run it ad hoc -- `npx -y github:Muhammadatef/kakashi mask <file>` -- read the diff before sharing, and wire nothing.

excluded.name: skills-cli
excluded.reason: Cross-agent skill installer + registry CLI (vercel-labs/skills @ 435076e78988e1e6ec40d00b0b1d76bdbbc5419a, npm `skills`, MIT, TypeScript, ~29.5k stars, active). `npx skills add <source>` installs SKILL.md packs from GitHub shorthand / any git URL / local path into 77 agents (claude-code, cursor, codex, opencode, …) as symlinks to a canonical copy under .agents/skills/, tracked in a gitignored skills-lock.json; plus find/update/remove/init/use and the skills.sh registry. License-clean, mature, in-category infrastructure — NOT wrong-category — but Ignore for the catalog on three grounds. (1) Channel overlap: for Claude Code its job is already done by the plugin marketplace ai-kit itself ships through (self-contained plugin, v5.0.0), and running both channels on one pack produces live duplication — this repo's own skills-lock.json + .claude/skills/caveman* symlinks (npx-skills install of JuliusBrussee/caveman, 2026-05-22) still shadow the caveman PLUGIN that setup Branch 2e later wired, so every caveman skill appears twice in the session skill list. Exactly the failure the plugin-over-symlinks rule exists for. (2) Not a companion: one-off install tooling with zero per-session compounding value (catalog dimensions: graphify=input, caveman=output, llm-wiki=memory, context7=docs); scope is person/one-off, not project. (3) Publishing ai-kit ITSELF through it — considered and rejected: ai-kit skills call bin/ scripts, standards/ files and each other, so standalone SKILL.md installs would ship broken halves, and reach beyond Claude Code + Cursor is deliberately out of scope (same posture as ADR-0010's Copilot rejection). should-i-use verdict: Ignore (catalog). It keeps its existing role as the documented direct-install fallback for skill packs that are NOT Claude marketplace plugins — the role taste-skill's alternative field already gives it.
excluded.alternative: Claude Code packs: one channel only — the plugin marketplace; never run an npx-skills install alongside the same pack's plugin. Non-marketplace SKILL.md packs: `npx skills add <owner>/<repo>` ad hoc, as taste-skill's entry documents; wire nothing. When a plugin takes over a pack, delete the leftover npx-skills install (skills-lock.json + .claude/skills/<pack> symlinks + .agents/skills/<pack>) — this repo's caveman leftovers are the standing example.

excluded.name: autoresearch-universal
excluded.reason: Universal prompt-optimization loop skill (balukosuri/Andrej-Karpathy-s-Autoresearch-As-a-Universal-Skill, SHA 4870864, single SKILL.md + README + ARTICLE, no code). Applies the Karpathy autoresearch pattern to prompts: scan repo → binary eval criteria → autonomous generate-eval-score-mutate loop with llm-judge criteria, validation set, plateau breaker, mutation operators. Well-written loop design, but Ignored on four independent grounds: (1) ADR-0002 collision — the loop is agent-run LLM-in-the-loop evaluation, exactly what ai-kit declined twice (v1.1.0: no LLM-judge; 2026-07-26 #119 revisit: agent-run A/B is 'one step worse — real API cost AND non-determinism AND no CI gate'); ai-kit's skill-quality machinery is deliberately deterministic (tests/eval: 49 files of prompts+goldens, eval-structure.sh, eval-golden.sh, /ai:contribute-eval). (2) Scope — installs person-global (~/.claude/skills/), value hangs on 'whoever is optimizing a prompt, in any repo'; runs are one-off .autoresearch/ lab sessions, not per-project compounding infra like the companion catalog is for. (3) Trust/provenance — NO license (README's 'use it, modify it, share it' is not a grant; GitHub default all-rights-reserved), hard VETTING.md fail; provenance chain Karpathy → unnamed 'a YouTuber' → upload-only commits ('Add files via upload'), repo lived 2 days (2026-03-21→23) then dead; README documents autoresearch-universal/SKILL.md but the tree has SKILL.md at root — marketing-vs-code drift inside 3 files. (4) Overlap — skill-creator (already installed) covers eval/benchmark/optimize for skills; /ai:autonomous carries the autonomous-loop shape. should-i-use verdict: Ignore. No spike issue: ADR-0002's existing 'revisit when agent-run A/B becomes cheap and deterministic enough to gate CI' trigger already covers the only future in which this pattern fits.
excluded.alternative: Use ai-kit's deterministic eval layer (tests/eval goldens + /ai:contribute-eval) for skill regression, and skill-creator's eval/benchmark for interactive skill optimization. If someone personally wants an autoresearch-style prompt loop for a one-off, copy the SKILL.md to their own ~/.claude/skills/ — licence-unclear, so do not vendor any of its text into ai-kit.

excluded.name: google/mcp
excluded.reason: Google's MCP index repo (google/mcp, SHA 9ebafd607afdc06245323756a07221df23790a93, default branch main, Apache-2.0, 4.5k stars). Not a tool — whole repo is README.md + CONTRIBUTING + LICENSE + examples/ (two ADK demo apps: launchmybakery, allstrides). README is ~35 bullet links to Google's remote and OSS MCP servers plus Cloud Run hosting docs; each linked server lives in its own repo under its own licence (googleapis/gcloud-mcp, gemini-cli-extensions/*, ChromeDevTools/chrome-devtools-mcp), so the Apache-2.0 here covers only the README and the two examples. Ignored on four grounds: (1) Category overlap — ai-kit already owns this slot with standards/external/mcp-servers.json (24 signal-gated entries, pinned SHA 3449c10, derived from anthropics/claude-plugins-official) consumed by /ai:recommend-tools; google/mcp is the same category ungated and unscored, a list you read once in a browser. (2) Zero signal — grep -ril 'gcloud|google cloud|bigquery|cloud run|firestore|vertex ai|gke' across every .md/.json/.sh in ai-kit returns 0 hits; mcp-servers.json's cloud category is aws/cloudflare/vercel/coolify, and downstream projects (emeq, naschool = Laravel; emeq-web = Astro) are all self-host on Coolify per paas.json. Adding GCP entries would violate paas.json's own stated rule that the catalog 'grows from real adoption signal, not speculation'. (3) Maturity — README states verbatim 'This is not an officially supported Google product. This project is intended for demonstration purposes only' and 'This project is not eligible for the Google Open Source Software Vulnerability Rewards Program'; the google/ org name buys credibility the repo itself disclaims. VETTING.md maturity fail. (4) Scope = one-off — value is 'find out which Google MCP servers exist', consumed once, nothing to wire. Nothing installable: no package, no binary, no server. should-i-use verdict: Ignore.
excluded.alternative: If a project ever actually deploys to GCP, wire googleapis/gcloud-mcp (the real server) as a normal signal-gated mcp-servers.json entry — signals files: app.yaml / cloudbuild.yaml — not this index that merely points at it. File that from real adoption signal, not speculatively.

excluded.name: rtk
excluded.reason: CLI output compressor (rtk-ai/rtk @ 322db4da98219b15608d5b71eddf6338c48d693c, DEFAULT BRANCH `develop` not main, Apache-2.0, single Rust binary, ~77.5k stars, v0.28.2, active 2026-08-26). `rtk init -g` writes a PreToolUse Bash hook + RTK.md + a ~/.claude/settings.json entry; the hook rewrites `git status` -> `rtk git status` so the agent reads a compacted form of ls/tree/cat/grep/git/test/docker output. Despite the 'proxy' framing it is a per-command wrapper, not a daemon, and nothing sits in the path of prompts or responses. Ignore for the CATALOG, but it is NOT in the same class as the other six from this article: it is the first candidate that clears every objection that sank `headroom` in the same dimension. (1) Footprint: one static Rust binary + brew formula + clean `rtk init -g --uninstall`, vs headroom's Python 3.10 + HuggingFace Kompress-v2 + long-running proxy. (2) Trust: hooks only the Bash tool call, reads no credentials, exchanges no OAuth token, never auto-edits CLAUDE.md (writes its own RTK.md). (3) Overlap: it compresses tool INPUT-side output only, so it does not double caveman (model output) or graphify (code index). Marketing/code parity is unusually honest — README states the 60-90%% figure is bash output not bill, and that token counts are `bytes / 4` because it ships no tokenizer. Two real objections remain, both project-specific and both verified here: (a) LOSSY READS — `cat`/`read` are rewritten to 'signatures and structure over full bodies', and this repo's sessions route file reads through Bash (auto-mode), so an edit-after-read would act on a truncated body; ai-kit is 248 .sh + 365 .md files whose contents get read to be edited, which is the worst case for signature-only reads. (b) HOOK COLLISION — /ai:setup already wires `bin/hooks/search-delegation-check.sh` on PreToolUse `Bash|Grep|Glob` (130 lines, advisory, points wide sweeps at `graphify query` or a sub-agent); RTK adds a second global PreToolUse Bash hook that silently rewrites the same calls. Coexistence is plausible but unproven and would need a documented conflict check before any catalog entry. Scope is person-global (`-g`), same machine-wide activation shape ai-kit already accepts for caveman and ponytail. should-i-use verdict: Ignore (catalog) / spike. Folded into the open runtime-output companion question rather than filed as a new issue — see #110.
excluded.alternative: Do not add to the companion catalog on an article's say-so. The runtime tool-output dimension is genuinely open (graphify=input, caveman=output, llm-wiki=memory, context7=docs, ponytail=code — nothing owns bash output); #110 now carries rtk as the stronger candidate than headroom. To try it personally today: `brew install rtk && rtk init -g`, then read a shell script through Bash and confirm the body is not truncated before trusting it for edits. Uninstall: `rtk init -g --uninstall && brew uninstall rtk`.

excluded.name: context-mode
excluded.reason: Tool-output sandbox for coding agents (mksglu/context-mode @ 64c338814123e5326acdd7ae6fbaffff70fe6f9b, main, ~20k stars, active). Runs large tool outputs (test logs, DOM snapshots, GitHub payloads, MCP results, scraped pages) into a local sandbox + SQLite/FTS index and passes back only a summary plus retrieval handles; claims 98%% tool-output reduction; ships MCP + hooks across 17 platforms. Same dimension as rtk and headroom, and Ignored ahead of both on licence: LICENSE is **Elastic License 2.0**, not open source — GitHub reports it as NOASSERTION, and the text carries the standard ELv2 hosted-service ban plus 'you may not move, change, disable, or circumvent the license key functionality in the software'. A licence-key clause in a tool ai-kit would recommend to every project is a hard VETTING.md #1 fail; recommending it commits downstream projects to a commercial gate that can move. Secondary grounds match headroom's: MCP + hooks + persistent session memory spans three dimensions ai-kit already fills (graphify, llm-wiki, checkpoint/resume), and lossy pre-agent summarisation of tool output is a correctness gamble against ai-kit's verifiability posture. should-i-use verdict: Ignore. No spike — #110 covers the dimension, and rtk is the licence-clean candidate in it.
excluded.alternative: If the runtime-output dimension gets a companion, it should be the Apache-2.0 one (rtk, see #110), not an ELv2 tool with a licence-key clause. For large test/log output today, run the noisy command in a sub-agent (Explore / ai:explore / cavecrew-investigator) so the raw block lands in that context, which is what search-delegation-check.sh already nudges toward.

excluded.name: code-review-graph
excluded.reason: Local-first code intelligence graph (tirth8205/code-review-graph, main, MIT, ~30.9k stars, active). Tree-sitter parses functions/classes/imports/call edges/inheritance/test deps into SQLite, exposed over MCP + CLI for blast-radius and review queries. Structurally eligible, licence-clean, and genuinely good — but it is the SAME slot as `codebase-memory-mcp`, already Ignored above: an ALTERNATIVE to graphify, which is ai-kit's wired input-retrieval companion (CLAUDE.md rule, `graphify query` workflow, graph-fresh check in /ai:docs-sync, and the PreToolUse search-delegation nudge that names it by hand). Two knowledge-graph tools on one repo is double-bundle noise, and graphify already answers the article's own example question ('which files and tests does this change affect') from graphify-out/graph.json at zero API cost. MCP surface also runs against ADR-0006. should-i-use verdict: Ignore. Whether a stronger engine should REPLACE graphify is the existing spike, not a catalog add — #109, which now has two candidates (codebase-memory-mcp, code-review-graph) rather than one.
excluded.alternative: Keep graphify. If the replacement spike (#109) ever runs, evaluate code-review-graph alongside codebase-memory-mcp against the same bar: AST-derived and deterministic, zero per-update API cost, incremental update, and a computable staleness stamp (graphify's `built_at_commit`, which /ai:docs-sync reads).

excluded.name: token-savior
excluded.reason: Progressive code-reading MCP server (Mibayy/token-savior, main, MIT, ~1.1k stars; a bklieger-groq/token-savior lineage also exists — the article shows only a repo card, so the exact upstream is ambiguous, but the category verdict holds for either). Serves an index/symbol summary before full file bodies, plus a persistent memory engine; claims 97.9%% on a coding benchmark at -80%% active tokens. Ignore on overlap, not quality: 'summary before full body' is what graphify already provides (`graphify query`/`explain` returns a scoped subgraph instead of whole files), and the nudge to use it instead of reading blind is already wired as a PreToolUse hook — `bin/hooks/search-delegation-check.sh`, in this repo's own .claude/settings.json on matcher `Bash|Grep|Glob`. Its second half (persistent memory) doubles llm-wiki + .agents/memory + checkpoint/resume, so like headroom it spans dimensions rather than filling a gap. MCP server + benchmark-headline marketing with a single-maintainer repo also fails the promotion quorum and ADR-0006. should-i-use verdict: Ignore.
excluded.alternative: Use graphify for structure-before-body, and let the search-delegation hook route wide sweeps to `graphify query` or a sub-agent. Nothing to wire.

excluded.name: claude-context
excluded.reason: Semantic code-search MCP (zilliztech/claude-context, DEFAULT BRANCH `master`, MIT, ~12.4k stars). Chunks a repo, embeds it, stores vectors in Milvus/Zilliz Cloud, exposes search over MCP. Ignore on three independent grounds. (1) Same alternative-to-graphify slot as code-review-graph and codebase-memory-mcp; three tools competing for one wired dimension. (2) Cost + external dependency, verified in its own README: it requires BOTH a Zilliz Cloud API key (MILVUS_TOKEN, sign-up link is a utm-tagged referral) AND an OPENAI_API_KEY for the embedding model — so indexing this repo's 749 tracked files means recurring API spend and shipping source-derived embeddings to a third-party service, against graphify's AST-only, offline, zero-cost `graphify update .`. (3) Provenance of the recommendation: the source article is written by Milvus, and two of its seven picks (claude-context, memsearch) are Zilliz's own products with the piece closing on a Zilliz Cloud CTA — vendor content, weighted accordingly. should-i-use verdict: Ignore.
excluded.alternative: Keep graphify (AST-derived, offline, free, incremental). If a project ever genuinely needs embedding-based semantic search over code — 'find the concept, I don't know the symbol name' — that is a spike against graphify's limits (#109), not a catalog add, and it must be costed: embeddings API spend per index plus a hosted vector DB.

excluded.name: memsearch
excluded.reason: Cross-session agent memory (zilliztech/memsearch, main, MIT, ~2.5k stars, active; Claude Code plugin via `/plugin marketplace add zilliztech/memsearch`). Markdown files are the source of truth with Milvus as a rebuildable shadow index; captures every conversation turn automatically, offers 3-layer progressive recall (search -> expand -> transcript), hybrid dense+BM25+RRF. Design is genuinely close to ai-kit's own posture — markdown-first, human-editable, index derived — and it targets a REAL open pain here: #108, auto-memory MEMORY.md growing unbounded as checkpoints accumulate. Still Ignore, on footprint and overlap. Footprint: Python >=3.10 plus a ~558 MB ONNX bge-m3 model downloaded from HuggingFace on first launch plus a Milvus instance — the same shape as headroom's Python+HF stack, which ADR-0006 already rejected, for a repo that is pure Bash + Markdown. Overlap: memory is the one dimension ai-kit fills three times over (llm-wiki for non-code documents, .agents/memory/ for project/feedback/reference facts with /ai:hygiene's memory-audit for staleness, /ai:checkpoint + /ai:resume for session handoff); adding a fourth surface that auto-captures every turn also widens the trust surface, since everything typed is written to disk and embedded by default. Scope is person, not project: the value hangs on whoever is working, across all repos. should-i-use verdict: Ignore. Its one reusable idea — progressive recall, so a memory hit returns a summary and only drills to the transcript on demand — costs nothing to adopt natively and is the right shape for #108's unbounded-index problem.
excluded.alternative: Keep the existing memory stack. Fold the progressive-recall idea into #108 (MEMORY.md as the search layer, memory file as expand, session transcript as last resort) rather than installing an embedding stack for it. If someone personally wants automatic capture across every repo, install the plugin in their own global config — it does not belong in a project's wiring.

excluded.name: skill-doctor (warpdotdev/common-skills)
excluded.reason: Grades an agent setup by LLM-scoring local conversation history, then drafts diffs against your SKILL.md files and renders an HTML report (MIT (c) Denver Technologies, Python 3.9+ stdlib-only, evaluated at 09a28422e21904eaa721b9c1cebdd8eecc454e9c). Judged as a kit question: would ai-kit recommend this into a consuming repo like emeq-hub, naschool or emeq. No, on four grounds. (1) Duplicates a first-party feature the consuming developer already has: Claude Code ships native /skill-doctor and has already iterated past it, with skill usage and context costs moved to the Stats tab. `claude plugin eval --ablation with-without` answers 'did this skill fire' causally against a no-plugin baseline, where transcript scoring only observes correlation. (2) Vendor lead-gen in the developer loop: SKILL.md step 6 instructs the agent to finish EVERY response with a linked 'Request access to Warp Factories' line (cta_url at SKILL.md:148, mandate at :162-165), and the same CTA is stamped into the share PNG. ai-kit recommending that means shipping a vendor funnel into a client's repo. Stripping it makes the adoption a permanent fork. (3) Licence chain dead-ends: assets/pierre-diffs.js is 1,156,623 bytes of minified Shiki (91% of install size) with zero @license, copyright or THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES text anywhere in the repo (verified by fetching the blob and grepping it). Fails VETTING criterion 4, where the adopted diagram-design carved its bundled icon sets out explicitly. A kit cannot pass that on under an implicit 'safe to wire' endorsement. (4) Overlaps the chain ai-kit already ships INTO those repos: log-skill.sh + usage-stats.sh (coverage), ai-kit-hygiene.sh (Score: N/100 with a ranked fix recipe), contribute-eval (failure to permanent regression case), workflow/evals + eval.yml, whose cases are already in native plugin-eval format. Cost is roughly 250-300k tokens per run, paid by the consuming developer, against the posture of the v1.46.0 context-budget release. NOT a ground: an earlier draft of this entry claimed it finds 0 skills because it only scans .agents/skills, .claude/skills and .codex/skills. bootstrap-project.sh creates exactly those directories in every consuming repo (naschool 15, emeq-hub 11, emeq 3), so it would in fact find ai-kit's skills there. That objection was an artefact of evaluating ai-kit itself instead of a target project, and is retracted. should-i-use verdict: Ignore.
excluded.alternative: Point the consuming developer at native /skill-doctor, and run `claude plugin eval workflow --ablation with-without` for causal firing checks. Keep contribute-eval as the durable failure-to-test path. The gap it exposed, 3 eval cases for 40 skills, is ai-kit's own backlog item.

excluded.name: ui-skills
excluded.reason: Post-generation UI polish skill set (ui-skills.com; npm `ui-skills` v0.2.4, maintainer ibelick / motion-primitives; baseline-ui, fixing-accessibility, fixing-motion-performance). Installs via `npx ui-skills add`, not a Claude Code marketplace plugin, so it does not fit the plugins.json schema — the same structural reason taste-skill was excluded. Fails VETTING #7 (provenance): the published package.json carries no `repository`, `homepage` or `files` field, its `description` is a raw markdown image tag (`![UI Skills](./public/UI-OG.webp)`), and the tarball ships the whole Astro marketing site (68 files, 451 KB, `astro dev` / `astro build` scripts, Cloudflare adapter) rather than a CLI — there is no upstream repo to pin a SHA against. Substance overlaps standards/rules/a11y.mini.md (WCAG 2.2 AA, always-on); its perf half is covered better by web-quality-skills, which is measurement-first, MIT, and plugin-installable. should-i-use verdict: Ignore.
excluded.alternative: Use web-quality-skills for the measured a11y / perf / SEO pass and a11y.mini.md for the always-on rule. If a person specifically wants its polish pipeline, install it at person scope: `npx ui-skills add baseline-ui`.

excluded.name: frontend-design-toolkit (wilwaldon)
excluded.reason: Curated link list of frontend/design tooling for Claude Code (wilwaldon/Claude-Code-Frontend-Design-Toolkit, 810★, a single 29 KB README, no code, last pushed 2026-04-11). Nothing to install or wire. Fails VETTING #3 (marketing-vs-code parity) on its own content: it attributes Chrome DevTools MCP to Anthropic and prints the install `npx @anthropic-ai/chrome-devtools-mcp@latest`, a package that 404s on npm (real: `chrome-devtools-mcp`, ChromeDevTools/Google, Apache-2.0, 49.8k★); its UI/UX Pro Max star count contradicts itself inside the same file (62.6k in the section header vs 16.9k in the Quick Reference; actual 121.7k); the bencium entry points at a repo that redirects and carries no license; several 'Source' links resolve to aggregator sites rather than upstream repos; the README claims MIT while GitHub reports no license and the tree has no LICENSE file. Its own 'Essentials' and 'Solo Builder' stacks are already fully covered by ai-kit's catalog (frontend-design, ui-ux-pro-max, context7, playwright, typescript-lsp, chrome-devtools-mcp) — and ai-kit's chrome-devtools-mcp entry is the correct one. Mined for leads 2026-08-27: web-quality-skills adopted, ui-skills and taste-skill excluded, Figma MCP declined (owner does not use Figma). should-i-use verdict: Ignore.
excluded.alternative: Use ai-kit's own plugins.json / mcp-servers.json — they already carry this list's recommended stacks with correct install commands.

excluded.name: show-me (humanlayer/skills)
excluded.reason: Visual-explanation skill (humanlayer/skills, plugins/show-me, MIT, Copyright (c) 2026 HumanLayer, read at 3c2629142c5d437428269b1b722b08c0b87f574d). One 2.5KB SKILL.md, zero code, zero deps: seven ways to answer the current question with a picture instead of prose. Judged as a kit question, would ai-kit recommend installing this into a consuming repo like emeq-hub, and the answer is no, because there is nothing to install that ai-kit cannot own outright. It is an idea, not a tool. Wiring it would mean a second marketplace every developer has to add, upstream drift to track, and a macOS-only `open` to live with, all for 100 lines of markdown. Same shape as the technical-writing entry above: Ignore as a plugin, adopt the one durable layer as a pattern. Done at workflow/skills/show-me/SKILL.md (2026-08-27), which credits humanlayer in its provenance block. The text, decision table, rules and examples are ai-kit's, the view set and the smallest-view-that-answers rule are theirs. Deliberately absent from vendored.json, which tracks verbatim copies for bin/ai-kit-upstream-drift.sh to chase; a divergent reimplementation must never be resynced. should-i-use verdict: Ignore as a plugin, adopted as pattern.

excluded.name: claude-seo
excluded.reason: SEO/content-marketing ops bundle (AgriciDaniel/claude-seo, MIT, v2.2.5 @ a1480c7, 15.5k stars). 25 skills + 18 agents + ~54 Python scripts: technical SEO, E-E-A-T, schema, GEO/AEO, backlinks, local/ecommerce/international SEO, GSC/GA4. No derivation overlap with ai-kit (E-E-A-T / citability / hreflang / Search Console = 0 hits) — genuinely new material, but wrong category: ai-kit is a dev-lifecycle kit (plan-build-review-ship), not marketing ops. Same out-of-scope bucket as taste-skill and designlang. Judged against emeq-hub, which DOES have a real organic surface — public routes /, /partners, /partners/{provider} (programmatic, 2 providers), /support, 3 legal pages, plus dynamic SitemapController, RobotsController and LlmsController. It is already solved there to a higher standard than an audit tool delivers: App\Support\Seo\{SeoMeta,Schema} build canonical/OG/JSON-LD centrally, and tests/Feature/PublicSeoTest.php (264 lines, CI-gated) asserts the Organization/WebSite/BreadcrumbList/SoftwareApplication schema graph, visible-vs-structured FAQ parity, sitemap-vs-live-provider drift, legal dateModified, a non-production Disallow:/ staging-leak guard, and robots.txt 'Content-Signal: search=yes,ai-train=no,use=reference' with per-agent AI-training blocks. A CI assertion beats a periodic audit. The whole evaluation surfaced exactly one real gap, and it is a deploy-verification gap, not an SEO-knowledge gap: config/inertia.php throw_on_error defaults false (silent client-side fallback), every Inertia SEO assertion uses assertInertia (props, not rendered HTML), and `make ssr-check` — which already greps live HTML for hero copy — runs only against the local APP url from `make ssr`, never from `make deploy`, whose post-deploy check is `curl /up` only. Closable in ~3 lines with code already in the repo. Cost of adopting instead: 43 skill+agent descriptions in context, Python 3.10+ venv, Playwright Chromium, 18.7KB CLAUDE.md, PostToolUse hook spawning node->python on every Edit/Write (self-filters on content, no false blocks). Uncovered by emeq-hub and genuinely absent: keyword/SERP/competitor/backlink research and GSC field data — but a ~10-URL B2B integration surface is not a keyword-research problem. should-i-use verdict: Ignore.
excluded.alternative: Close the one real finding natively: call the existing `ssr-check` target from `make deploy` against the prod URL, and/or listen for Inertia\Ssr\SsrRenderFailed. If a pre-launch second opinion is ever wanted, install claude-seo globally, run `/seo audit` once, uninstall — one-off scope, wire nothing per-project.

excluded.name: notebooklm-py
excluded.reason: Unofficial Python API + agentic skill for Google NotebookLM/Gemini Notebook (teng-lin/notebooklm-py, MIT, 19k★, 2191 commits). Drives Playwright browser automation for auth plus undocumented internal Google endpoints for the actual calls — the README itself discloses this: 'undocumented Google APIs that can change without notice... APIs may break... Best for prototypes, research, and personal projects.' That self-scoping is the verdict: research category already covered for project use by llm-wiki, firecrawl, exa (standards/external/companions.json, mcp-servers.json), none of which sit on an unofficial scrape of a consumer web app or store a personal Google session. Fails VETTING #8 (security) on posture, not on a scan finding: Playwright-driven login against a personal Google account is a credential/session-storage surface no catalog entry should normalize project-wide. should-i-use verdict: Ignore for the catalog.
excluded.alternative: Person-scope only, if wanted: install globally, point it at a personal Google account, never wire into a project's .claude/ config. For project-scoped research/synthesis, use the existing llm-wiki / firecrawl / exa entries.

excluded.name: hyperframes
excluded.reason: HTML-to-MP4 video renderer for AI agents (heygen-com/hyperframes, Apache-2.0, HEAD 0fd70b1d, 43k★, active — HeyGen production use, tldraw/TanStack adopters). Ships as 20 `npx skills add`-installed agent skills plus a standalone CLI; headless-Chrome-seek + FFmpeg-encode, deterministic output. Clean licence, real traction, no bundled-dependency landmine — but wrong category for ai-kit's catalog: output is a rendered marketing/promo video, i.e. marketing-content production, not dev-lifecycle tooling (plan-build-review-ship). Same out-of-scope bucket as the claude-seo exclusion above. Unlike ui-ux-pro-max/diagram-design (whose output feeds back into the product itself — UI code, docs diagrams), a promo MP4 does not. Surfaced from a personal need spanning 4 repos (emeq-web, emeq-app, emeq-hub, planny) — person-scope (same operator, work doesn't hang on any one repo's stack), not project-scope, which is a second reason it doesn't belong as a per-project catalog companion. should-i-use verdict: Ignore for the catalog.
excluded.alternative: Person-scope tool: run `npx hyperframes init` + `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes --skill <workflow>` (scope to the one needed creation workflow — a non-interactive add without `--skill` installs all 20) whenever any of the 4 apps needs a video. Don't wire it as standing tooling into any single project's AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md.

excluded.name: herdr
excluded.reason: Rust-binary agent-aware terminal multiplexer — persistent sessions, JSON socket API for agent-to-agent orchestration, install via `curl -fsSL https://herdr.dev/install.sh | sh` or `brew install herdr`, released ~March 2026. Provenance is unclear: search for the canonical repo returns at least four separately-orged copies with byte-identical descriptions (ogulcancelik/herdr, motionharvest/herdr, creator-engine/herdr-ce, SuperCodeAgents/herdr-terminal) — no single repo confirmed as upstream, and a `curl | sh` install from an unpinnable source is exactly the supply-chain risk VETTING.md's provenance-SHA + security-scan criteria exist to catch, but they cannot be applied when there is no one source to pin. Fails Track B question 1 regardless of provenance: which terminal multiplexer you run is scope=person (whoever's terminal, any repo) — same bucket the six-part verdict table reserves for 'their own global install', never per-project catalog infra. ai-kit's own concurrent-agent story (`/ai:autonomous`'s `.agents/worktrees/<branch-slug>`, vendored Sandcastle `sequential-reviewer`) is one-worktree-per-issue, drained sequentially — not N simultaneous agents in one terminal — so the file-collision problem herdr solves doesn't exist in ai-kit's own workflow. should-i-use verdict: Ignore.
excluded.alternative: Personal terminal choice, not project infra. If genuinely wanted, verify the actual upstream repo (not one of the duplicate copies) before running any install script, at person scope only.

excluded.reason: General-purpose Rust terminal multiplexer (zellij-org/zellij, MIT, established, KDL layout format v0.40+). Real, unambiguous upstream — no provenance concern like herdr. Still scope=person: which multiplexer you run in your own terminal is not project-shaped, same reason tmux/screen were never catalog candidates. Checked companions.json/plugins.json/mcp-servers.json/hooks-patterns.json for a terminal-multiplexer entry — zero hits, none belong there. should-i-use verdict: Ignore.
excluded.alternative: Personal choice, install globally if wanted (`brew install zellij`). Not project infra.

excluded.name: caffeinate
excluded.reason: macOS-bundled sleep-prevention utility (Apple, ships with every Mac, zero install). Not a catalog candidate in any sense — nothing to Wire or Vendor, it is already on every macOS machine. Scope is machine/person: whether a laptop sleeps mid-run depends on the operator's hardware, not this repo. Checked ai-kit's own AFK-run surface (`/ai:autonomous` SKILL.md, `docs/spikes/aikit-autonomous-ralph.md`) for a real gap — neither mentions sleep or session-persistence risk, so there is a genuine one-line documentation opportunity (a `caffeinate -s -- ...` operator tip for long unattended runs) but that is a doc tweak, not a catalog entry, and wasn't applied without being asked. should-i-use verdict: Ignore for the catalog.
excluded.alternative: Not applicable — already installed everywhere. Optional: add `caffeinate -s --` as an operator tip in `/ai:autonomous`'s usage docs if unattended-run laptop-sleep ever becomes an actual complaint.

excluded.name: hunk (hunkdiff)
excluded.reason: Terminal diff viewer for agent-authored changesets (OpenTUI + Pierre diffs; npm `hunkdiff`, canonical repo likely modem-dev/hunk per hunk.dev, requires Node 18+). Same provenance red flag as herdr: search returns near-identical descriptions ('Review-first terminal diff viewer for agentic coders') across PodJamz/hunk--diff-viewer, modem-dev/hunk, dporkka/diffhunk, smolcars/hunk, WilliamTaack/hunk-tui-diff — five separately-orged copies, no clean single provenance to pin a SHA against. Its one genuinely novel idea — a `.hunk/notes.json` file-based two-way review channel the agent reads via `hunk notes list` and writes via `hunk notes add` — duplicates the contract surface ai-kit already committed to: the GH issue/PR body is the deliberate review-feedback channel (see the openspec exclusion above), and `/ai:autonomous`'s `exit-gate review-blocked` routes to human review through that same GH surface, not a local JSON file. The multi-file diff-attribution pain it targets (which of N concurrent agents touched which file) doesn't fire in ai-kit's own workflow either — autonomous is one-worktree-per-issue, sequential, so diffs are already branch-isolated, not commingled. should-i-use verdict: Ignore.
excluded.alternative: Keep GH PR/issue comments as the review-feedback channel. If a project runs genuinely concurrent multi-agent work needing a local structured-diff reviewer, verify the actual upstream repo first, then install person- or task-scoped — not project infra.

excluded.reason: shadcn/ui-style registry of React video-composition components (`npx shadcn add framecn/...`) — 'animated in code, renderable to MP4', built on Editframe (a paid cloud video-render SaaS: client-side SDK / browser render / CLI render tiers, billed per minute streamed via their Premium Player). Scope is person/one-off, same as hyperframes: value hangs on whoever needs a video, in whatever repo, not ai-kit's own workflow. Adds a cost dimension hyperframes doesn't: hyperframes self-hosts (headless Chrome + FFmpeg, free); framecn is a thin UI layer over a paid third-party render service, so adopting it means recurring Editframe spend on top of the component install. should-i-use verdict: Ignore for the catalog.
excluded.alternative: Person/one-off scope: if a specific app has a real, current video need, evaluate framecn + Editframe's actual pricing tier in that project's own context (see the hyperframes entry's precedent — Track B lives at the consuming repo, not ai-kit). Don't wire it as standing tooling into any project's AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md.

excluded.reason: 24/7 autonomous 'AI company' daemon (MaxMiksa/Auto-Company, main@ebfab9b4bd5f0ab5ad452a1ff85285b3c141acdd, MIT, Python, 2728★). Wraps Claude Code or Codex CLI in a continuous launchd/systemd loop: 14 expert-persona subagents (CEO=Bezos, CTO=Vogels, Marketing=Godin, CFO=Campbell, etc.) form dynamic 3-5 person squads each cycle to ideate, validate, build, deploy and market products under `projects/`, with near-zero human input — the only steering surface is editing `memories/consensus.md`'s 'Next Action' between cycles. Nothing in ai-kit's own repo has a 'ideate a product, deploy it, market it' pain point — no `path`/count in this repo this would touch, so Track B fails at question 1. Footprint if it were ever wired: Python runtime, launchd/systemd daemon, local dashboard, bypassPermissions/danger-full-access by default — the same broad-access-daemon posture ADR-0006 already rejects (headroom, codebase-memory-mcp exclusions above). should-i-use verdict: Ignore for the catalog — wrong category (whole application, not dev-lifecycle companion) and no consuming-project pain observed.
excluded.alternative: Scope is person/one-off if it's ever relevant at all: someone wanting to run an autonomous multi-agent product-builder for a side project should run Auto-Company standalone in its own directory, not wire it into ai-kit or any consuming project's AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md. ai-kit's own multi-agent needs stay served by `/ai:autonomous` (GH-issue-gated, worktree-per-issue) and the subagents.json Agent Teams pattern.

excluded.reason: Offensive bug-bounty / external red-team skill bundle (elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter, main@f032240d876c40465770ab4839e7257b9e7254e8, MIT, 4031★, active — pushed 2026-09-01, created 2026-05-05). No category-taxonomy gap check applies either: adding a 'security' bucket for this one entry would be inventing a new catalog dimension nobody asked for. Track B (ai-kit as the consuming repo) fails at question 1 — ai-kit is a meta-tool with no deployed app, API, or auth flow of its own to hunt bugs against; no path or count in this repo this would touch. Scope is person/one-off: value hangs on whoever is running an authorized bug-bounty or red-team engagement, in whatever target and repo, not on this project's stack — same bucket as the framecn/auto-company exclusions above. should-i-use verdict: Ignore for the catalog.
excluded.alternative: Scope is person/one-off: a specific downstream project with a live deployed surface and an actual authorized engagement (bug bounty program, pentest contract) should install it directly at that project — `/plugin marketplace add elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter` then `/plugin install claude-bughunter@elementalsouls` — as person/task tooling, not wired into ai-kit or recommended as standing per-project infra. Keep the built-in `security-review` skill for defensive pre-merge review of pending diffs.

excluded.reason: Community reference guide + example `.claude/` config (wesammustafa/Claude-Code-Everything-You-Need-to-Know, main@d9e93740193aeae2cd661c7ddf6f0c8f8989860b, MIT). Not an installable plugin — no `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, no server code — it's a docs repo (README + docs/reference/*.md on hooks/skills/subagents/effort-levels/models/agent-teams) plus copy-paste example files: 4 notification/stop hook scripts with TTS glue (ElevenLabs/OpenAI/pyttsx3), 9 specialized-agent role prompts (backend/frontend/db/ux/security-reviewer/business-analyst/project-manager/tech-lead + an orchestration canvas), 7 slash commands, 4 MCP-server writeups (memory, playwright, sequential-thinking, serena), a claude-md-review skill, and GH hygiene (issue templates, PR template, stale-link Action). Checked ai-kit's own catalogs by derivation, not name: hooks-patterns.json already ships `permission-prompt-alert` + `idle-prompt-alert` (Notification-event, universal) — same trigger the repo's TTS hooks fire on, so its contribution there is one voice-narration implementation, not a new pattern category. `/ai:setup-gh-workflow` already installs issue templates + PR template + DoR/DoD-enforcing workflows, a stricter version of the repo's static templates + link-checker Action. `/ai:docs-sync` already covers dead-link + repo-hygiene + finished-work checks, a superset of the repo's `stale-docs-audit.js`. mcp-servers.json has 24 entries but not `memory`/`sequential-thinking`/`serena` — checked value, not just absence: memory MCP is redundant with the harness's own file-based memory system already active every session, sequential-thinking MCP is a prompting pattern largely superseded by native extended thinking, and serena (LSP-based semantic code search) overlaps graphify (already a companion) plus the harness's own deferred `LSP` tool. One real gap found: `.claude/skills/claude-md-review/SKILL.md` is a dependency-free (Read/Glob/Grep only), ~90-line skill auditing CLAUDE.md for vagueness, dead-path references, staleness, conflicts and bloat — distinct from `/ai:hygiene`'s context-lean check, which only flags CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md over 200 lines and says nothing about content quality. should-i-use verdict: Ignore the repo as a whole for the catalog (wrong shape — reading material + examples, not a wireable tool); the claude-md-review skill is the one Adopt-as-pattern candidate it surfaces, queued separately rather than folded into this Ignore.
excluded.alternative:
The claude-md-review gap is queued via `/ai:to-prd` Defer mode (`--label catalog-candidate`) rather than implemented inline here. If picked up: reimplement natively as a new workflow/skills/ entry (credit the source), run it past VETTING.md first, and route it alongside `/ai:hygiene`'s context-lean check rather than replacing it — one checks length, the other checks content.

Track B, checked against the actual consuming repos (emeq-hub, emeq-app, emeq-hub-sdk, planny) rather than assumed from ai-kit's own catalog: still Ignore, now on repo evidence instead of assumption. Notification/TTS hooks — none of the 4 repos have a Notification-event hook wired at all; ai-kit's own `permission-prompt-alert`/`idle-prompt-alert` sits unused everywhere, so the gap (if it's real) is a wiring gap, not something this repo's Python/ElevenLabs implementation would add. Specialized-agent personas — emeq-hub (`consumer-scope-auditor`, `partner-api-factchecker`) and emeq-app (`pencil-reviewer`) already run bespoke, domain-specific agents that outclass generic role personas; no pain evidence at emeq-hub-sdk or planny (both zero custom agents) to justify adding one speculatively. memory/sequential-thinking/serena MCP — graphify already runs in emeq-hub, emeq-app and emeq-hub-sdk (3 of 4); only planny lacks it, which is a graphify-adoption gap unrelated to this repo. claude-md-review's one concrete trigger — emeq-hub-sdk's CLAUDE.md at 244 lines, over ai-kit's own 200-line context-lean floor — turned out to be a false positive on inspection: ~176 of those lines are Laravel Boost's auto-generated `<laravel-boost-guidelines>` block (`php artisan boost:install --guidelines`), not authored bloat. emeq-hub already solved this exact failure mode with a cheaper fix: `CLAUDE.md` just does `@AGENTS.md` (Boost writes to AGENTS.md via `config/boost.php`, not to CLAUDE.md directly) with a guard comment telling the next agent to restore the import if Boost's output ever lands inline — no review skill needed, and any adopted claude-md-review would need to special-case generated blocks to avoid the same false positive it just produced here.

reversed.name: ponytail
reversed.now: Wire — companions.json, universal, auto-prompted via Branch 2e (2026-08-26)
reversed.reason: The original Ignore rested on one claim: redundant with ai-kit's own always-on `pre-write-discipline.mini.md`, so wiring ponytail would mean two always-on rulesets double-injecting the same discipline. That claim was false and was never verified when the entry was written. Re-checked 2026-08-26 against the code: `workflow/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` declares NO hooks key, `bin/lib/emitters/claude-code.sh` writes rules to `.claude/rules/<name>.md` described in its own header as 'read by agent on demand', and `.claude/rules/` does not exist in this repo at all. `default_mode: always-on` is a frontmatter label with no delivery mechanism behind it ON CLAUDE CODE — 30 rules carry it (22 in standards/rules/, 8 in standards/rules/feedback/), 21 of them universal, and none inject there. There was never any double injection to avoid on that host. IMPORTANT SCOPE CORRECTION, caught in pre-release review: the label IS load-bearing on Cursor, where bin/lib/emitters/cursor.sh maps always-on to `alwaysApply: true` in the emitted .mdc. So the mode is dead weight on one host and real enforcement on the other. ponytail injects for real at SessionStart + SubagentStart (all three hooks call getPonytailInstructions()), and SubagentStart covers what rules structurally cannot — every builder/designer/debugger subagent. Against VETTING.md, next to caveman which was already adopted: licence MIT with no carve-outs (caveman is MIT + BSL-1.1 on its Engine directories, a non-OSS tag that was missing from its own catalog entry until this same change added it); benchmark suite checked in with named baselines and numbers the author revised DOWN after issue #126 criticism; 112k stars / 63 contributors / 6160 forks vs caveman's 101k / 33. Security (VETTING #8): skillspector static scan over the whole repo returns DO_NOT_INSTALL, risk 100, 27 HIGH — all of it noise, triaged and rejected. ZERO findings land in the shipped runtime (hooks/, skills/, bin/); every HIGH sits in benchmarks/, tests/, README.md or docs/. Two sampled HIGHs: 'Agent Snooping' on the README table that honestly documents which files ponytail writes, and 'Anti-Refusal' on the phrase 'without judgment' inside a benchmark result about path-traversal safety. Hand-read of hooks/*.js: no network, no child_process, no credential env reads — only ponytail's own config vars and host-detection vars. Cost, measured not assumed: SKILL.md is 120 lines / ~1.4k tokens, injected at SessionStart and SubagentStart. UserPromptSubmit does NOT inject the full body in Claude Code — only in the Qoder branch and on explicit /ponytail commands.
reversed.consequence: `pre-write-discipline.mini.md` KEEPS `default_mode: always-on`. It was briefly flipped to on-demand on the theory that ponytail had taken over the always-on slot; pre-release review caught that this would emit `alwaysApply: false` into every Cursor project's .mdc while ai-kit's ponytail wiring is Claude-Code-only — stripping the discipline from Cursor with nothing replacing it. The flip was reverted. ponytail and the rule are complementary per host, not a hand-off: ponytail enforces on Claude Code, the mode enforces on Cursor. The broader finding — `always-on` means enforcement on Cursor and nothing on Claude Code, for the same 30 rules — is NOT fixed by this change and is tracked in #144.
